I would keep my planting plan simple and familiar. In Quzhou County, the safest base for me is still the wheat and summer maize rotation, because I know how to manage it, the market is steady enough, and the land and water conditions fit it. At my age, I would not want to spread myself too thin with too many complicated cash crops. I would put most of my land into winter wheat followed by summer maize, then keep a smaller piece for peanuts so I have some cash income and some rotation benefit. I would use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stability, but I would not chase anything too fancy. For tillage, I would mostly use rotary tillage because it is practical and manageable, and I would keep fertilizer at moderate levels instead of pushing too hard, especially with nitrogen, because input costs matter and I would rather aim for stable output than gamble on very high yields. I would irrigate wheat more than maize and peanuts, because wheat here depends more on timely water. For crop protection, I would spray only as much as I think is necessary to control the main diseases, insects, and weeds, not more. My whole approach would be steady, familiar, labor-manageable, and based on protecting yield without raising risk too much.
